newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close higher, consolidation seen.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close higher, consolidation seen.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed slightly higher on Friday in mixed trading with no single dominant factor, and brokers said consolidation was likely due to weakening market energy.
"Liquidity in the market began falling again," said Na Min-ho, a broker at Daishin Securities.
The composite index ended 0.91 of a point at 695.67.
Brokers said financial troubles of the Jinro Group were weighing on the market, limiting any steep index rises.
Jinro said it would reduce its subsidiaries to about 10 from 24 through mergers or sales.
Volume totalled 38.74 million shares, against 42.93 million on Thursday. Decliners and advancers were almost level 387 to 383, with 136 unchanged.
Customer deposits with securities houses were estimated at 3.1 trillion won as of Thursday, down slightly from 3.12 trillion on Wednesday, brokers said.
Jinro held a briefing session on Friday for possible buyers of its real estate, factories and buildings put on sale.
Jinro, the nation's 19th largest conglomerate, or chaebol, wants to sell unprofitable business lines and other assets because of financial difficulties.
Jinro Ltd, a liquor unit of the group, closed flat at 9,600 after fluctuating between 8,850 and 10,100.
Brokers said Jinro had still difficulties getting fresh loans from non-bank institutions.
Shares of garment maker New Star Trading Co Ltd went limit-up on its move to thwart a takeover bid by Seoul-based Savoy Hotel, brokers said.
The company said it would buy back five percent of its own common shares between April 21 and July 20 to defend against a takeover bid by Savoy.

Savoy bought 11.11 percent of New Star's outstanding shares in the open market on April 9-10, raising its stake in the firm to 24.7 percent. The hotel said on Friday it planned to raise the stake to 51 percent to take over New Star's management.
Hours later, New Star said it was seeking a white knight to ward off the corporate raider.
Brokers said the planned expansion on May 2 of the foreign stock ownership ceiling to 23 percent from 20 percent would help improve sentiment next week.
